summary: René Guénon (1886–1951) was a scholar in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at the Robert-Badinter School Complex (1902–1903), Collège-lycée Jacques-Decour (1904–1906), and the University of Paris (1914–1917).

René de Nebesky-Wojkowitz (1923–1959) worked in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Vienna (Dr. phil. 1946–1949; Habilitation ~1953–1955), Berlin, SOAS (~1950–1953), and LSE under Koppers, Haekel, Bleichsteiner, Tucci, and Rock, later serving at Weltmuseum Wien (1958).
René de Saussure (1868–1943) worked in linguistics and other fields. He studied at Johns Hopkins University (~1893–1895) and held a teaching post at the University of Geneva (~1898–1900).
Richard A. Gard (1914–2007) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a professor at the Institute for the Advanced Study of World Religions and was its director (attested 1982–1989).

Richard A. Hutch (1945–) is a religious studies scholar who studied at Gettysburg College (~1963–1967), Yale Divinity School (~1967–1970), and the University of Chicago (~1970–1974). He held posts at Southern Illinois University and the University of Queensland (~1978–2010).

Richard A. Rosengarten is a religious studies scholar at the University of Chicago, where he served as Dean (attested 2008–2012) and as Associate Professor of Religion and Literature, including in the College (attested 2026).
Richard B. Martin (1937–1996) worked in Indology and Tibetology. He held posts at the University of Virginia as a professor (attested 1983–1991) and South Asian bibliographer (attested 2003).

Richard Baker (1936–) is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Harvard and UC Berkeley, and under Shunryu Suzuki. He founded the San Francisco Zen Center (1962), serving as its abbot (1971–1984), and founded Dharma Sangha.
Richard Barron is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche, Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima, and Jamgon Kongtrul III.

Richard Bowring (1947–) is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Cambridge (BA, doctorate, Litt.D), and held posts at Columbia, Princeton, Selwyn College (Master 2000–2012), and Cambridge, where he became Emeritus Professor (1985).

Richard Carnac Temple (1850–1931) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. Educated at Harrow and Trinity Hall, Cambridge, he served in the Bengal and Indian Staff Corps, edited the Indian Antiquary (~1884–1921), and was vice-president of the Hakluyt Society.
Richard D. Mann is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned his PhD at McMaster University under the supervision of Phyllis Granoff (attested 2003).

Richard D. McBride II works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at UCLA mentored by Robert E. Buswell Jr., held a fellowship at Washington University in St. Louis, and held a post at Dongguk University (attested 2012).

Richard Delbrueck (1875–1957) was an archaeology and history scholar. After studying at the University of Bonn (~1895–1899), he held academic posts at Bonn (~1902–1908), Jena as Professor of Archaeology (~1917–1928), and Giessen (~1928–1930).

Richard F. Nance is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago (-2004) and held Assistant (attested 2013) and Associate Professor (attested 2026) posts at Indiana University Bloomington.

Richard Fick (1867–1944) was an Indologist who completed his doctorate at Kiel University (~1885–1888). He worked at Kiel University Library, the Prussian State Library, and served as director of Göttingen State and University Library (~1921–1932).

Richard Foltz (1961–) works in Iranian/Central Asian studies, religion, and history. Educated at Utah and Harvard (PhD ~1991–1996), he taught at Brown, Columbia, Kuwait, and Florida, and became Founding Director of Concordia University's Centre for Iranian Studies (~2006–2026).
Richard Fritzsche (1851–) was an Indology scholar who studied under Hermann Brockhaus (~1874–1877) and served as Rektor at Gymnasium Schneeberg (attested 1976).

Richard Gombrich (1937–) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Oxford under Robert Charles Zaehner, Walpola Rahula, and Gananath Obeyesekere. He served as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford and Balliol College (1965/1976–2004).

Richard Hartshorne (1899–1992) studied at Princeton University (~1916–1920) and the University of Chicago (~1920–1924). He held faculty posts at the University of Minnesota (~1924–1940) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1940–1970).
